original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation constructs semantic IDs for catalog items and predicts the next ID from user interaction histories. However, existing methods face limitations in both stages. First, conventional quantizers may produce imbalanced code assignments and lack coherent intermediate semantic units between individual tokens and complete items, limiting history reconstruction. Second, recommendation models remain dominated by next-item prediction, treating historical interactions mainly as conditioning context and providing limited supervision for recovering persistent preferences across the historical path, particularly when relevant preference signals are distributed over distant interactions. To address these limitations, Structure-Aligned History Learning (SAHL) reconnects the two stages by using the structure created during quantization directly for history reconstruction. Its Semantic Residual Balanced Quantization (SRBQ) forms a balanced token-subspace-item hierarchy, and SAHL reconstructs history at these same granularities. Predictive entropy prioritizes uncertain transitions, while curriculum optimization progressively shifts training to inference-aligned next-item prediction. On four Amazon Review categories, SAHL improves NDCG@10 by 18.6%-30.0% over RPG and 2.7%-6.0% over strong method MHL. Controlled analyses verify balanced code use, the benefit of following quantizer-defined groups during reconstruction, and dependence on user history. The relevant code is available at https://github.com/CQU-MM-Intelligent-Lab/SAHL.
original_abstract.source_title: Structure-Aligned History Learning with Subspace-Structured Semantic IDs for Generative Recommendation

en.text: SAHL aligns history reconstruction with a balanced token–subspace–item hierarchy learned by semantic residual quantization. Predictive entropy emphasizes uncertain transitions, and a curriculum shifts training toward next-item prediction. On four Amazon Review categories, NDCG@10 improves by 18.6–30.0% over RPG and 2.7–6.0% over MHL. The evidence concerns code utilization and history-dependent offline recommendation, without demonstrated industrial latency or CTR gains.

zh.text: SAHL 用语义残差均衡量化建立 token—子空间—商品层次，并沿同一结构重建用户历史；预测熵用于突出不确定的转移，课程训练逐步转向与推理一致的下一商品预测。在四个 Amazon Review 类别上，NDCG@10 相对 RPG 提升 18.6%–30.0%，相对 MHL 提升 2.7%–6.0%。证据集中于编码利用率与依赖历史的离线推荐，未验证工业延迟或 CTR 收益。

original_abstract.text:
Vector search engines built on cloud object storage have drawn growing attention from both academia and industry. These systems typically adopt a disaggregated storage-compute architecture, persisting the primary vector payload in object stores (e.g., Amazon S3) while retaining compact index metadata on compute nodes. However, conventional vector indexing structures are not natively tailored to the pronounced network latency and per-request access costs of cloud object stores, resulting in network I/O amplification, degraded query throughput, and higher API expenses.
  To resolve these challenges, we present RemoteANN, a vector search engine explicitly co-designed for cloud object storage across indexing and querying. To mitigate the dominant network I/O bottleneck, RemoteANN couples an Inverted File (IVF) index with RaBitQ quantization, further optimized by inter-cluster and intra-cluster data reordering for improved data locality. Building on this tailored data layout, RemoteANN's query engine combines cluster pruning, fine-grained Range-GET requests, request merging, and local NVMe SSD caching, dramatically reducing discrete storage requests and network transfer volume without sacrificing accuracy. To address the index construction bottleneck, we further develop QGKMeans, which substantially reduces construction latency without compromising clustering quality. Extensive evaluations on real-world datasets demonstrate that, compared with representative baselines, RemoteANN achieves up to a $5.9\times$ throughput speedup while issuing up to $16.1\times$ fewer object storage requests at 97% target recall.
original_abstract.source_title: RemoteANN: A Native Vector Search Engine for Cloud Object Storage

en.text: RemoteANN co-designs vector indexing and querying for cloud object storage, combining IVF and RaBitQ with locality-aware reordering, cluster pruning, Range-GET merging and NVMe caching. QGKMeans reduces index construction latency. At 97% target recall, evaluations report up to 5.9x throughput and 16.1x fewer object-storage requests than representative baselines. This supports infrastructure choices for large vector retrieval; recommendation-quality gains are not established.

zh.text: RemoteANN 面向云对象存储协同设计向量索引与查询，将 IVF、RaBitQ 量化与局部性重排、簇剪枝、Range-GET 合并及 NVMe 缓存结合，并用 QGKMeans 降低建索引延迟。在目标召回率 97% 时，相对所测代表性基线，吞吐最高提升至 5.9 倍，对象存储请求数最多减少至约 1/16.1。该结果可供大规模向量检索基础设施参考，未证明推荐质量提升。

original_abstract.text: Hybrid architectures offer a promising approach to efficient language modeling by combining a small number of full-attention layers with a larger number of efficient sequence layers, such as sparse attention and recurrent layers. While full-attention layers maintain a KV cache that grows linearly with sequence length, efficient layers typically rely on separate, fixed-size states rather than accessing this richer existing memory. Recent work has begun exploring ways to allow efficient layers access to the KV cache, but the theoretical benefits of such access, and the extent to which existing approaches can realize them remain poorly understood. We investigate these questions by analyzing the expressive power of individual hybrid blocks on function composition, a well-studied task in sequence-model expressivity associated with multi-hop reasoning. We first establish that both conventional hybrid blocks and those with top-$κ$ KV-cache access require $Ω(\sqrt{n})$ capacity to compute even two-function composition over a domain of size $n$. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the \emph{Multi-hop Retrieval Attention} (MuRA) hybrid block, a simple architecture that enables multi-hop retrieval from a shared KV cache while preserving asymptotic computational and memory efficiency. We prove that a single fixed size $m$-hop MuRA block can compute $m$-function composition, whereas computing $(m+1)$-function composition with the same retrieval depth requires polynomial model size, establishing a strict expressivity hierarchy in retrieval depth. Synthetic experiments support this hierarchy, showing that increasing retrieval depth enables learning progressively deeper compositions, substantially outperforming existing hybrid architectures. Together, our results identify multi-hop retrieval as a promising mechanism for improving the expressive power of efficient hybrid architectures.
original_abstract.source_title: Improving the Expressive Power of Hybrid Sequence Models via Multi-Hop Retrieval

en.text: MuRA lets efficient hybrid sequence layers perform multiple retrieval hops over a shared KV cache. For function-composition tasks, theory establishes a strict hierarchy in retrieval depth: a fixed-size m-hop block computes m-function composition, while one more composition requires polynomial size at that depth. Synthetic experiments support the hierarchy. This motivates more expressive efficient architectures, but does not establish language-model or recommendation production gains.

zh.text: MuRA 让高效混合序列层在共享 KV 缓存上执行多跳检索。函数复合任务的理论分析给出严格的检索深度层级：固定大小的 m 跳模块可计算 m 重函数复合，而保持该深度再多复合一层需要多项式规模。合成实验支持这一层级。它为增强高效架构的表达能力提供思路，但没有证明语言模型或推荐生产环境收益。

original_abstract.text: Micro-expert pruning reduces the capacity of mixture-of-experts (MoE) models by removing coupled channels within routed experts. However, finer pruning granularity alone does not guarantee the preservation of downstream capabilities, as similar language-modeling perplexity can accompany substantially different task performance. We revisit micro-expert mask construction as two distinct decisions: allocating retained capacity across experts and selecting channels within that capacity. We propose UC-RAMP, a two-stage post-training pruning framework that explicitly separates these decisions. CAPE uses cross-domain calibration evidence to redistribute expert widths under an exact layer-wise budget, while RAMP refines channel composition at fixed widths through one-out, one-in exchanges guided by a channel-interaction surrogate. Across three MoE models at 25% and 50% routed-expert channel pruning, UC-RAMP achieves the highest ten-task mean accuracy among evaluated pruning methods in five of six settings. At 50% pruning, it outperforms the strongest evaluated baseline by 8.19, 3.96, and 6.14 percentage points across the three models, respectively. In a single-A100 deployment at 25% pruning, UC-RAMP reduces measured time to first token by 19.7--23.9% and time per output token by 20.2--22.3% relative to the unpruned model. The code is available at https://github.com/xzktx003/UC_RAMP.
original_abstract.source_title: Fine-Grained Units, Flat Decisions: Hierarchical Micro-Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Models

en.text: UC-RAMP separates allocation of retained expert widths from channel selection in post-training MoE pruning. CAPE redistributes capacity under an exact layer budget; RAMP refines channels at fixed widths using interaction-guided exchanges. It has the best ten-task mean accuracy in five of six tested model/pruning settings. At 25% pruning on one A100, time to first token falls 19.7–23.9% and time per output token 20.2–22.3% versus unpruned models. Transfer to recommendation remains untested.

zh.text: UC-RAMP 将 MoE 训练后剪枝分成专家宽度分配与通道选择两步：CAPE 在固定层预算内重新分配容量，RAMP 再依据通道交互替换通道。它在六种模型与剪枝比例组合中的五种取得最高十任务平均准确率。单张 A100、25% 剪枝时，相对未剪枝模型，首 token 延迟下降 19.7%–23.9%，每输出 token 耗时下降 20.2%–22.3%。这些压缩方法尚未在推荐任务上验证。

original_abstract.text: Accurate product discovery on the Web requires recommendation models that rank catalog candidates within tight inference budgets. In semantic-ID recommendation, deployment can fuse code probabilities with item similarities, making the final ranking depend on their normalization and relative weights. This motivates a direct training principle: \emph{distill what you rank}. We present OneChord, which uses one learned, catalog-normalized fusion for next-item supervision, refinement distillation, and inference. A shared parallel decoder produces joint SID evidence and item-matching scores. During training, a frozen denoiser supplies legal partial SIDs; the student evaluates these states to construct refined fused targets. Matching direct and refined predictions on shared hard candidates transfers refinement into one-pass recommendation. We characterize the fusion weights induced by candidate conditioning and establish sufficient conditions for preserving the refined predictor's full-catalog Top-$K$ selection. Across six Amazon datasets, OneChord achieves the highest Recall@5 and NDCG@5 among the compared methods on every dataset, with average relative gains of 6.30\% and 7.12\% over the strongest baseline. It also achieves a 1.04--1.18$\times$ full-test generation speedup over the fastest baseline. OneChord makes the served ranking distribution the common object of recommendation learning and distillation.
original_abstract.source_title: OneChord: Distill What You Rank, Recommend in One Pass

en.text: OneChord uses the same learned, catalog-normalized fusion of semantic-ID and item-matching scores for supervision, refinement distillation and serving. A parallel decoder learns from refined targets on shared hard candidates so that inference needs one pass. Across six Amazon datasets, average Recall@5 and NDCG@5 gains over the strongest baseline are 6.30% and 7.12%; full-test generation is 1.04–1.18x faster than the fastest baseline. These are offline recommendation results, with no reported production CTR test.

zh.text: OneChord 在监督训练、细化蒸馏与服务时使用同一套经过全目录归一化的分数融合，将语义 ID 概率与商品匹配分数对齐。并行解码器在共享困难候选上学习细化目标，把多步细化能力压入单次前向推理。在六个 Amazon 数据集上，相对最强基线的 Recall@5、NDCG@5 平均提升 6.30%、7.12%；完整测试集生成速度为最快基线的 1.04–1.18 倍。这些是离线推荐结果，未报告生产 CTR 测试。

original_abstract.text: Looped transformers reuse a shared block of layers to increase computational depth without increasing the number of trainable parameters. They are trained with backpropagation through time (BPTT). To save training compute, BPTT is often truncated to the last few loops, although this may weaken the benefit of looping. To study this tradeoff systematically, we jointly vary model size, training tokens, and forward and backward loop counts across nearly 600 training runs and fit a unified scaling law that captures the effects of looping and truncation through effective parameters. Despite the training-compute savings of truncation, our fitted law favors full BPTT when forward and backward loop counts are jointly optimized. In matched-compute runs, full BPTT through fewer loops consistently outperforms truncated settings of the same compute. The law further shows that at fixed model size, the compute-optimal loop count and training-token budget both grow with compute. When model size is also free, the law identifies two fully trained loops as the best looped setting. Experimentally, this setting achieves lower loss than the compute-optimal non-looped model with about 27% fewer non-embedding parameters and only 8% more training compute.
original_abstract.source_title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation

en.text: Across nearly 600 looped-Transformer training runs, the study models the joint effects of model size, data, forward loops and backward loops. When both loop counts are optimized under matched compute, full backpropagation through fewer loops outperforms truncation. With model size also variable, two fully trained loops achieve lower loss than the compute-optimal non-looped model using about 27% fewer non-embedding parameters and 8% more training compute. The result informs loop-training budget allocation within the studied language-model regime, not validated CTR scaling.

zh.text: 研究通过近 600 次循环 Transformer 训练，联合分析模型大小、数据量及前向和反向循环次数。在相同计算预算下同时优化两种循环次数时，较少循环配合完整反向传播优于截断反向传播。允许调整模型大小后，两次完整训练循环相比计算最优的非循环模型，以约少 27% 的非嵌入参数和多 8% 的训练计算获得更低损失。结论可用于所研究语言模型范围内的循环训练预算分配，尚未在 CTR 上验证。

original_abstract.text: Generative retrieval assigns each item a discrete semantic identifier (SID) and retrieves items by autoregressively generating SID sequences. In dynamic environments such as e-commerce, new items arrive continuously, requiring periodic updates to the SID-to-Item mapping and model to maintain retrieval timeliness. Each update, however, can invalidate search paths already learned by the retriever, and the quantitative relationship between mapping change and retrieval quality has not been systematically characterized. We study this problem with extensive controlled experiments over 67 days of large-scale e-commerce search logs and obtain three core findings. (1) SID semantic drift causes severe retrieval degradation that may be masked by large beam sizes: mapping updates reduce HitRate by 41.78-62.05% at beam size 1 but only 8.33-10.85% at beam size 1000, as redundant candidate generation conceals the true severity of drift. (2) The fraction of changed SIDs is strictly monotonically related to retrieval quality: as the remapped fraction increases from 0% to 72.75%, HitRate decreases monotonically, dropping up to 42.66% at beam size 1. Full remapping remains substantially worse than the preservation policy under warm-start training, indicating that short-budget continued training alone cannot repair topology disruption. (3) The SID topology-preserving principle makes even the simplest warm-start strategy highly effective: fixing old-item SIDs, inserting new-items, and warm-starting from the previous model improves old-item HitRate by 10% and new-item HitRate by 109%, validated across two non-overlapping update cycles. These findings distill into a concise deployment principle: insert new-items, freeze old-items; warm-start when possible, otherwise freeze; never change SIDs the model has already learned. A three-week online A/B test on TmallAPP shows UCTCVR +0.29% and GMV +1.16%.
original_abstract.source_title: Don't Rewrite the SID Map: Topology Preservation for Generative Retrieval in Dynamic E-Commerce Search

en.text: The study links semantic-ID remapping to retrieval degradation using 67 days of e-commerce logs. Large beams conceal much of the damage: at beam size 1, mapping updates reduce HitRate by 41.78–62.05%. Preserving old-item IDs, inserting new items and warm-starting the model improves old- and new-item HitRate by 10% and 109% across two update cycles. A three-week TmallAPP A/B test reports UCTCVR +0.29% and GMV +1.16%. These findings support stable identifier topology in the tested dynamic retrieval setting.

zh.text: 研究基于 67 天电商搜索日志，分析语义 ID 重映射造成的检索退化。大束宽会掩盖部分损失；束宽为 1 时，映射更新使 HitRate 下降 41.78%–62.05%。固定旧商品 ID、插入新商品并热启动模型，在两个更新周期中分别提升旧商品和新商品 HitRate 10% 与 109%。天猫 App 三周 A/B 测试报告 UCTCVR 提升 0.29%、GMV 提升 1.16%，支持在该动态检索场景中保持 ID 拓扑稳定。

original_abstract.text: Click-through rate (CTR) prediction underpins recommender systems and online advertising, where high-dimensional categorical features interact in combinatorially many ways. Several recent CTR models, such as FinalNet and QNN, report higher accuracy when a network also learns from its own averaged predictions, for example by running the same network under different dropout patterns and training each run toward the average. Why this self-distillation helps, and whether its random sampling is needed, remains unclear. This work shows that as the number of dropout patterns grows without bound, the objective reduces exactly to the label loss of the logit-averaged prediction plus a penalty on how much the dropout copies of the network disagree. When dropout does not affect how a network gates its features, this penalty can be approximated in closed form, and FLMNet is designed on this principle and trains without sampling. Networks trained from different seeds disagree in the same form, and distilling several of them into one network recovers part of their ensemble gain. On five benchmarks against seventeen baselines, the resulting models take the top two places in accuracy with a single network at inference, and the gains of the penalty and of distillation, where measurable, largely add up.
original_abstract.source_title: FLMNet: Self-Ensemble Distillation from Masks to Seeds for Single-Tower CTR Prediction

en.text: FLMNet explains dropout self-distillation as a label loss plus a disagreement penalty in the infinite-mask limit. When dropout leaves feature gating unchanged, the penalty admits a closed-form approximation, enabling sampling-free training; distilling models trained from different seeds recovers part of the ensemble gain in one network. On five CTR benchmarks against seventeen baselines, the resulting models occupy the top two accuracy positions. The evidence concerns benchmark accuracy with single-network inference, not industrial scaling laws.

zh.text: FLMNet 将无限多 dropout 掩码下的自蒸馏目标分解为标签损失与预测分歧惩罚。在 dropout 不改变特征门控的条件下，惩罚项可作闭式近似，从而免去训练时的随机采样；再把不同随机种子训练出的模型蒸馏到单个网络，保留部分集成收益。在五个 CTR 基准、十七个对比方法中，所得模型占据准确率前两名，推理仍只需一个网络。证据限于这些基准，未建立工业扩展规律。

original_abstract.text: Large-scale search and recommendation systems derive much of their retrieval quality from rich, heterogeneous features, yet existing generative retrieval (GR) methods struggle to exploit such feature ecosystems efficiently. Static feature injection either encodes all available signals or places them according to predetermined schemes, increasing serving cost and introducing irrelevant or conflicting evidence. More fundamentally, existing methods cannot adaptively determine when a feature is needed, which feature to select, or where it should influence hierarchical Semantic ID (SID) generation. We propose Agentic Generative Retrieval (AGR), a tool-augmented paradigm that interleaves SID generation with on-demand feature acquisition. Conditioned on the request and decoded SID prefix, AGR decides whether to invoke a tool, which feature to acquire, and where its observation should influence subsequent decoding, thereby steering generation toward feature-consistent SID branches. To supervise this behavior, we construct tool-augmented trajectories based on feature applicability and information gain along the SID hierarchy, and train the model through SID pretraining followed by tool-augmented fine-tuning. Experiments on an industrial dataset and three public benchmarks, together with an online A/B test, consistently demonstrate the effectiveness of AGR.
original_abstract.source_title: AGR: Agentic Generative Retrieval with Tool-Augmented Search

en.text: AGR interleaves semantic-ID generation with on-demand feature acquisition. The request and decoded prefix guide when to call a tool, which feature to fetch and where to use it; training trajectories use feature applicability and information gain. The abstract reports gains on an industrial dataset, three public benchmarks and an online A/B test, without numerical effect sizes. The work addresses feature-use cost and relevance in generative retrieval.

zh.text: AGR 在生成语义 ID 的过程中按需获取特征：根据请求和已生成的前缀，决定何时调用工具、获取哪项特征，以及在哪里使用它。训练轨迹依据特征适用性与信息增益构建。摘要报告了工业数据、三个公开基准和在线 A/B 测试中的效果，但未给出增益数值；其直接价值在于改善生成式检索的特征使用成本与相关性。

original_abstract.text: We propose KronLSTM, a linear attention architecture based on the Kronecker Delta Rule, a novel update rule for associative matrix memories. KronLSTM extends the xLSTM family with a memory-revision mechanism that corrects targeted associations while modifying the memory only along a single direction in matrix space. This minimally invasive memory revision reduces interference with previously stored information compared with delta-rule updates, making it particularly well suited for long-context language modeling. The resulting memory dynamics can be mathematically described as a Markov chain that converges to a steady-state distribution, while the expected norm of the memory matrix remains uniformly bounded throughout the entire input sequence. Hence, KronLSTM ensures stable memory dynamics without requiring additional normalization and stabilization mechanisms for the memory state. Experiments show that KronLSTM is competitive with, and often outperforms, existing linear attention architectures, including models of the (Gated) DeltaNet family, with particularly strong performance on long context benchmarks. These results establish the Kronecker Delta Rule as an effective and analytically tractable foundation for stable associative memory in recurrent linear attention architectures. Our code (https://github.com/NX-AI/KronLSTM) and models (https://huggingface.co/collections/NX-AI/kronlstm) are open-source.
original_abstract.source_title: Kronecker Delta Rule for Long Context Linear Attention

en.text: KronLSTM introduces the Kronecker Delta Rule, which revises associative matrix memory along one matrix-space direction to reduce interference with stored information. Its analysis establishes a uniformly bounded expected memory norm and steady-state convergence under the described dynamics. Long-context language-model experiments are competitive with, and often outperform, tested linear-attention baselines including the (Gated) DeltaNet family. This is a potentially transferable stable-memory design; recommendation performance has not been tested.

zh.text: KronLSTM 提出 Kronecker Delta Rule，沿矩阵空间的单一方向修正关联记忆，以减少对已存信息的干扰。论文分析给出了所述动力学下记忆范数期望的一致有界性与稳态收敛性质。长上下文语言模型实验与包括 (Gated) DeltaNet 在内的线性注意力基线相当，并在多项比较中更好。其稳定记忆机制可作为迁移候选，但尚未验证推荐效果。

original_abstract.text: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is increasingly served across geo-distributed cloud and edge infrastructures, where wide-area latency, cross-region egress cost, and data-residency rules compete with retrieval quality. Conventional pipelines rank by semantic similarity alone and ignore where content lives, inflating tail latency and cost. We formalize the Geo-RAG Selection Problem (GRaSP), a drop-in re-scoring layer that decays relevance by latency and adds an optional cost penalty under a cardinality budget and per-region caps, with no retraining. We first settle its complexity: the base formulation is a linear objective over a partition matroid, solved optimally by an O(N log N) greedy algorithm, rather than NP-hard as a knapsack framing suggests, with hardness entering only under an additive egress budget. On a five-node CloudLab testbed emulating a four-region WAN over the Natural Questions corpus (2.68M passages), GRaSP's benefit is placement-dependent: under uniform placement it cuts fetch latency at negligible quality cost; under topical (residency-like) placement it traces a recall-latency Pareto frontier that dominates relevance-only, nearest-k, and a latency-budgeted baseline. At a moderate latency setting, GRaSP lowers P90 fetch latency by 41% while retaining 78% of relevance-only's recall, with sub-millisecond selection overhead, stable to 200 queries/s. Findings generalize across four public BEIR benchmarks. In end-to-end question answering, GRaSP reduces context-fetch latency by 43% while remaining within 0.062 absolute EM of relevance-only retrieval.
original_abstract.source_title: GRaSP: Latency-Aware Optimization for Geo-Distributed Retrieval-Augmented Generation

en.text: GRaSP reranks retrieval candidates using relevance, network latency and optional transfer cost under regional caps, without retraining. Its benefit depends on content placement. On a five-node testbed, a moderate setting reduces P90 fetch latency by 41% while retaining 78% of relevance-only recall. End-to-end QA reduces context-fetch latency by 43% while staying within 0.062 absolute EM of relevance-only retrieval; this is a quality-latency trade-off.

zh.text: GRaSP 在区域数量约束下结合相关性、网络延迟和可选传输成本重排候选，无需重训；收益取决于内容部署位置。五节点测试平台上的中等延迟设置使 P90 获取延迟下降 41%，保留仅按相关性检索的 78% 召回率。端到端问答的上下文获取延迟下降 43%，EM 与仅按相关性检索的绝对差距不超过 0.062；这是质量与延迟的权衡。

original_abstract.text: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models reduce computation through sparse expert activation, but deployment still requires storing a large number of expert parameters. We study post-training expert pruning using task-domain calibration data as a subset-selection problem: given a pretrained MoE layer, select a fixed number of experts that best reconstruct its original output. Exact subset search is combinatorial and becomes intractable for modern MoE models with many experts per layer. We develop OptEP, a scalable continuous relaxation that directly optimizes differentiable expert-selection variables, followed by a lightweight reconstruction-based update of the retained expert weights. Across multiple MoE architectures and tasks spanning mathematical reasoning and code generation, our approach improves over the strongest existing expert-pruning baselines, with absolute accuracy gains of up to 15.05% on Qwen3-30B-A3B, 14.55% on Qwen3-235B-A22B, 11.06% on GLM-4.5-Air, and 16.20% on Mixtral-8x7B. The improvements are particularly pronounced under aggressive pruning, demonstrating that reconstruction-driven expert selection and weight adaptation can preserve substantially more of the original model's performance while reducing the number of retained experts.
original_abstract.source_title: Reconstruction-Optimized Expert Pruning for Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

en.text: OptEP treats post-training MoE expert pruning as selecting a fixed-size subset that reconstructs the original layer output. A continuous relaxation optimizes expert selection, followed by lightweight updates of retained weights. Across mathematical-reasoning and code-generation tasks, it outperforms evaluated pruning baselines, especially at aggressive pruning. The method targets expert storage costs; its abstract does not establish recommendation gains or measured serving acceleration.

zh.text: OptEP 将 MoE 训练后专家剪枝表述为固定数量的专家子集选择，以重建原层输出为目标。它先用连续松弛优化专家选择，再轻量更新保留的权重。在数学推理和代码生成任务上，它优于所评测的剪枝基线，激进剪枝时优势更明显。该方法针对专家存储成本，摘要没有证明推荐收益或实测服务加速。

original_abstract.text: Dense bi-encoders and late-interaction retrievers are usually treated as alternatives, yet they fail on different queries: one vector captures what a text is about, token-level matching finds its exact entities and phrases. Using both today means two models, two indexes and a score-fusion step. We present UIBK-Embedding-v1, a 179M-parameter English encoder that produces both representations in one pass and scores them with one unmodified MaxSim. The dense embedding is written into the list of token vectors as three extra vectors, and a one-dimensional tag keeps the two kinds of vectors from matching each other, so that plain MaxSim equals the token-level MaxSim plus a weighted dense cosine. The model therefore runs in a standard late-interaction index without changes; we test it with PLAID. A shared 18-layer trunk with a separate 4-layer top per head, and a cross-encoder distilled into the fused score, turn the two heads into one retriever. On BEIR, UIBK-Embedding-v1 reaches 59.79 nDCG@10. This is 2.57 points above LateOn, the strongest model of its size, and 2.10 points above it when both models read documents of the same length; UIBK-Embedding-v1 is ahead on all 15 datasets. On a decontaminated version of BEIR it stays ahead on average (61.55 against 60.36) and on 8 of 12 datasets. Among the 156 models with complete BEIR results in the MTEB results repository, only models with at least 1.5B parameters score higher. Code, model weights, and a technical blog post are available at https://github.com/DataScienceUIBK/uibk-embedding , https://huggingface.co/DataScience-UIBK/uibk-embedding-v1 , and https://huggingface.co/blog/abdoelsayed/uibk-embedding-v1 .
original_abstract.source_title: UIBK-Embedding: Effective Text Retrieval by Unifying Dense and Late-Interaction Retrieval

en.text: UIBK-Embedding combines dense and token-level retrieval in one 179M-parameter encoder and one unchanged MaxSim index. Three extra vectors encode the dense representation, with a tag preventing cross-type matching; shared layers and fused-score distillation train both heads together. BEIR nDCG@10 reaches 59.79, exceeding LateOn by 2.10 points under matched document lengths. On decontaminated BEIR it leads on average and on eight of twelve datasets.

zh.text: UIBK-Embedding 在一个 1.79 亿参数编码器和无需修改的 MaxSim 索引中结合稠密检索与 token 级检索。三个额外向量承载稠密表示，类型标记防止跨类型匹配，共享层和融合分数蒸馏联合训练两个分支。BEIR nDCG@10 达到 59.79；文档长度一致时，比 LateOn 高 2.10 点。在去污染版 BEIR 上，它的平均表现更高，并在十二个数据集中的八个领先。

original_abstract.text: Generative recommendation predicts items by autoregressively generating semantic identifiers (SIDs), whose tokens are shared across semantically related items. With this paradigm gaining adoption, the question of how to support unlearning in it has become pressing. If training interactions must later be removed, such as injected spam or interactions with items a user no longer wants, this sharing lets an unlearning update unintentionally affect the predictions for the interactions' neighbors. We show that this effect is locally structured and hidden by global metrics: unlearning can leave recommendation utility on the whole test set nearly unchanged while substantially degrading it on neighborhoods of the forgotten interactions' SIDs. We propose Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning (NAU), which augments interaction-level unlearning with explicit control over the probability mass assigned to the forgotten items' neighborhoods. Across three datasets and four SID tokenizers, NAU restores spam-induced exposure toward the retrained reference while retaining more than 95% of retrained utility, and recovers the neighborhood utility that forget-and-repair unlearning loses at no global cost. We identify local probability redistribution as an important failure mode of unlearning in SID-based generative recommenders and show that explicitly controlling this redistribution can mitigate its effects.
original_abstract.source_title: Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning for Generative Recommendation

en.text: Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning addresses collateral damage when shared semantic-ID tokens couple forgotten interactions to neighboring items. It explicitly controls probability mass in those neighborhoods alongside interaction-level unlearning. Across three datasets and four tokenizers, it moves spam-induced exposure toward a retrained reference while retaining more than 95% of retrained utility, and recovers neighborhood utility lost by forget-and-repair unlearning without reducing global utility.

zh.text: Neighborhood-Aware Unlearning 针对语义 ID 共享 token 导致的遗忘连带损伤，在交互级遗忘之外显式控制相邻商品的概率质量。在三个数据集、四种分词器上，它使垃圾交互引起的曝光变化向重新训练的参考模型回归，同时保留超过 95% 的重训效用；还能恢复“遗忘后修复”方法损失的邻域效用，而不降低整体效用。

original_abstract.text: Multi-vector retrieval models such as ColBERT often outperform single-vector models of comparable scale by matching queries and documents at the token level. However, retaining a vector for every token substantially increases storage requirements and slows retrieval compared to single-vector bi-encoders, limiting their scalability. We introduce FLINT (Fixed-budget Late INTeraction), an architecture that uses attention-based pooling to represent each query and document with a fixed number of embedding vectors. Unlike architectures that pool only document representations while retaining token-level queries, FLINT applies pooling symmetrically to both sides, limiting document storage and the number of vector comparisons needed during retrieval. FLINT achieves comparable ranking effectiveness to the closest baselines on BEIR and outperforms them on several benchmarks with longer and more complex queries, including BrowseComp+, CRUMB, and TREC Tip-of-the-Tongue 2025. We demonstrate that FLINT's effectiveness-efficiency benefits extend across encoder architectures, testing it on two separate backbones (BERT and ModernBERT). On long-query corpora, FLINT delivers 1.5-2.8 times faster end-to-end retrieval than ConstBERT, the closest baseline. FLINT also reduces index size by 5.3-9.3 times relative to token-level late-interaction models such as ColBERTv2.
original_abstract.source_title: FLINT: Fixed-budget Late Interaction

en.text: FLINT reduces multi-vector retrieval storage and comparison costs by attention-pooling both queries and documents into fixed vector budgets. It retains comparable BEIR effectiveness and improves several long-query benchmarks across BERT and ModernBERT backbones. On long-query corpora, end-to-end retrieval is 1.5–2.8 times faster than ConstBERT; index size is 5.3–9.3 times smaller than token-level late-interaction models such as ColBERTv2.

zh.text: FLINT 用注意力池化将查询和文档都压缩到固定数量的向量，降低多向量检索的存储和比较成本。在 BERT、ModernBERT 两种骨干上，它保持相近的 BEIR 效果，并改善多个长查询基准。长查询语料上的端到端检索速度为 ConstBERT 的 1.5–2.8 倍；索引比 ColBERTv2 等逐 token 交互模型缩小 5.3–9.3 倍。

original_abstract.text:
DrugCLIP places small molecules and protein pockets in one space, turning genome-wide drug discovery into large-K retrieval by vector proximity. A campaign fixes over 20K pockets in advance for one library of over 500M molecules. Each pocket keeps K = 500K candidates, 0.1% of the collection, versus 100 in ANN benchmarks. Missed hits never get tested, so mean recall must reach 99% relative to exact search. Large answers make IVF probe every list holding a result and graph search track K or more candidates, so costs grow with K. On our CPUs and GPUs, neither index family reaches the target without losing most of its edge over scanning.
  SweepANN partitions compressed vectors across GPUs and scans each resident partition. One matrix multiplication scores each block for a whole query batch, reading it once. Several plans perform the K-dependent selection and merging of each query's K answers, each returning an exact top-K under compressed scoring. The window plan retains each query's best K from sampled blocks as its seed, and only rows above each seed's minimum score, shared once across GPUs, enter the buffers.
  Four Blackwell GPUs (RTX PRO 6000) answer all 26,562 pockets with a resident time of about 61 seconds, excluding library loading, and 99.6% mean recall relative to exact FP32 search. DrugCLIP reports roughly 24 hours with eight A100 GPUs in its own campaign. On 500M rows, the window plan runs 1.41x faster than SweepANN's grouped plan in the same memory. Across 25M-500M rows and K of 10K-500K, all GPU IVF configurations meeting the recall target take 8.2-24x SweepANN's resident time. On DEEP1B's 1B vectors across eight GPUs, against SweepANN's exact full-score scan of uncompressed FP32 rows, the window plan cuts resident time by 5.4x and 3.2x at K = 100K and 500K. It also cuts per-GPU peak memory by 6.0x and 5.3x, losing 1.0 and 0.7 mean-recall points.
original_abstract.source_title: SweepANN: A GPU-Accelerated Large-K Approximate Vector Search for Drug Discovery

en.text: SweepANN targets large-K vector retrieval, where conventional ANN indexes lose much of their advantage at high recall. It scans compressed GPU-resident partitions with batched matrix multiplication and selective top-K merging. Four RTX PRO 6000 GPUs process 26,562 drug-discovery queries in about 61 seconds at 99.6% mean recall, excluding library loading. The application is drug discovery; cross-hardware campaign comparisons do not isolate an algorithmic speedup.

zh.text: SweepANN 针对高召回率、大 K 向量检索中常规 ANN 索引优势缩小的问题，用批量矩阵乘法扫描 GPU 驻留的压缩分区，并选择性合并 top-K 结果。四张 RTX PRO 6000 GPU 约用 61 秒处理 26,562 个药物发现查询，平均召回率为 99.6%，时间不含向量库加载。应用场景是药物发现；跨硬件的整体任务对比不能单独证明算法加速幅度。

original_abstract.text: As model parameters scale up, sparsely activated Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches have become essential for model scaling. However, mainstream models currently adopt hierarchical architectures, where experts in different layers, although topologically independent, exhibit substantial similarity and redundancy in their stored content. Compared to the hierarchically arranged \textbf{Local Expert} in existing mainstream models, we hypothesize that inter-layer shared \textbf{Meta Expert} hold greater potential. To this end, we conduct a multi-dimensional empirical comparison between Local and Meta Experts, and find that models incorporating Meta Experts exhibit lower parameter redundancy, together with lower cross-entropy loss and higher downstream task accuracy. With the activated quantity and the expert granularity held fixed, \textbf{our model matches the performance of Vanilla MoE using only 70--80\% of the experts}, substantially improving the model's scaling potential. Beyond removing inter-layer redundancy among experts and improving information storage efficiency, our theoretical analysis further shows that, compared with Local Experts, Meta Experts provide hidden states with more flexible residual pathways, thereby improving information retrieval efficiency.
original_abstract.source_title: Meta Expert: Cross-Layer Expert Sharing for Storage- and Retrieval-Efficient MoE

en.text: Meta Expert addresses redundant expert parameters across MoE layers by sharing experts between layers. Empirical comparisons show lower redundancy, lower cross-entropy and higher downstream accuracy; with activated expert count and granularity fixed, it matches vanilla MoE performance using 70–80% of the experts. The analysis attributes additional benefits to more flexible residual paths. These findings concern general model architecture, with no recommendation-specific evaluation.

zh.text: Meta Expert 通过跨层共享专家，减少 MoE 不同层之间的参数冗余。实验显示冗余和交叉熵更低、下游准确率更高；在激活专家数量与专家粒度不变时，使用原始 MoE 的 70%–80% 专家即可匹配其表现。分析还将部分收益归因于更灵活的残差路径。证据来自通用模型架构，没有推荐专门评测。

original_abstract.text: Modern industrial ranking systems increasingly adopt generative recommendation (GR) paradigms, in which user behavior sequences and non-sequential (NS) features are tokenized and jointly modeled by Transformer-style backbones. This unified formulation provides a scalable interface for modeling long histories and heterogeneous features. However, sequence and NS representations often carry asymmetric semantics: historical representations may combine environment context with observed-action semantics, whereas candidate-side NS representations contain no observed action but incorporate richer supplementary context, such as user-item interaction features and recent behavior lists. Direct interaction between such representations can make query-key dot products compare different semantic objects, limiting meaningful cross-token interaction. To fill this gap, we propose EASformer, an Environment-Action-State disentangled architecture for industrial app ranking. EASformer constructs an explicitly aligned context environment space shared by historical and non-sequence tokens, while disentangling user actions from historical token and candidate-specific context form non-sequence tokens. Based on this aligned space, EASformer enables complementary historical action retrieval and state-conditioned action prediction. Furthermore, the disentangled design supports a Cloze-style self-supervised objective by masking historical actions and reusing the candidate prediction pathway. On an offline benchmark from a real-world industrial app marketplace, EASformer achieves an AUC of 0.89411, yielding a 0.88% relative improvement over the deployed baseline. Online A/B tests further support this advantage, with relative eCPM lifts of 1.26% and 3.94% across two real-world ranking scenarios.
original_abstract.source_title: EASformer: Environment-Action-State Alignment for Industrial Generative Ranking

en.text: EASformer addresses semantic mismatch between historical behavior tokens and candidate-side features by separating environment, action and state representations. An aligned environment space supports action retrieval, state-conditioned prediction and masked-action self-supervision. On an industrial app-marketplace benchmark, AUC reaches 0.89411, a 0.88% relative gain over the deployed baseline; two online ranking scenarios report relative eCPM gains of 1.26% and 3.94%.

zh.text: EASformer 针对历史行为 token 与候选侧特征的语义不对齐，将环境、动作和状态表示分开。共享环境空间支持动作检索、状态条件预测及掩码动作自监督。在工业应用商店基准上，AUC 达到 0.89411，比线上基线相对提升 0.88%；两个在线排序场景的 eCPM 分别相对提升 1.26% 和 3.94%。

original_abstract.text: Semantic ID (SID)-based generative recommendation retrieves items through successive token-level decisions, making personalization at each decoding step essential. However, existing methods insufficiently account for prefix-dependent user evidence and imbalanced historical interaction loads among candidate branches. This can cause irreversible branch-selection errors and favor popular paths. We propose SPAR, a generative recommendation framework that jointly improves stepwise personalization and SID construction. Its PATH Decoder retrieves prefix-relevant evidence from compressed long-term user memories and combines it with recent behavior, user profiles, and event context to guide each token decision. Its RQ-PIB module balances historical interaction loads among sibling branches under each parent prefix while preserving semantic structure. Experiments on large-scale Youku production data show an average relative HitRate improvement of 2.66% over the strongest baseline. SPAR also increases target-prefix retention by 5.79 percentage points and reduces the traffic-weighted largest child-branch share by 32.84% across SID levels. In a 7-day online A/B test, SPAR serves 10% of Youku's production traffic and improves average watch time per user by 3.95% and play conversion rate by 3.38%. These results demonstrate more reliable hierarchical decoding, balanced SID branches, and improved user engagement in industrial recommendation.
original_abstract.source_title: SPAR: Stepwise Personalized Autoregressive Recommendation with Prefix-Balanced Semantic IDs

en.text: SPAR addresses irreversible branch errors and popularity-heavy paths in semantic-ID generation. Its PATH decoder retrieves prefix-relevant evidence from compressed user memories, while RQ-PIB balances interaction loads among sibling branches. On Youku production data, relative HitRate improves by 2.66% over the strongest baseline. A seven-day A/B test covering 10% of traffic reports watch time per user +3.95% and play conversion +3.38%.

zh.text: SPAR 针对语义 ID 生成中的不可逆分支错误和热门路径偏置，用 PATH 解码器从压缩用户记忆中检索与当前前缀相关的证据，并用 RQ-PIB 平衡同级分支的交互负载。在优酷生产数据上，HitRate 比最强基线相对提升 2.66%；覆盖 10% 流量的七天 A/B 测试报告人均观看时长提升 3.95%、播放转化率提升 3.38%。

original_abstract.text:
Sparse attention reduces the computational cost of long-sequence video Transformers, but three-dimensional token layouts often leave selected blocks partially occupied, wasting physical tile capacity. We present KPage, a block-sparse attention scheme that packs valid 16-row K/V pages across logical-block boundaries into large tiles directly during loading, without materializing compacted tensors in high-bandwidth memory. KPage also routes Q blocks between 64x256 and 128x128 tiles to reduce query-side padding. Exact masking and K/V-owned page packing preserve the original sparse graph in forward and backward execution.
  Across five representative workloads, KPage achieves 1.35x-2.06x bare forward-kernel speedup over NVIDIA Block-Sparse Attention (BSA), with a geometric mean of 1.77x. It is near parity for fully occupied blocks (1.03x) but achieves 2.29x geometric-mean speedup on 3D layouts with partial blocks. KPage reduces physical query-key pair capacity from 334.1G to 177.5G while preserving 160.6G useful interactions. Across eight layouts from open-source SSTA, STA, and VSA systems, KPage achieves 1.13x-4.25x forward and 1.02x-2.71x forward-plus-backward speedup over the strongest exact sparse baselines. With independent Q/K partitions, KPage also achieves 1.49x speedup over the strongest exact sparse baseline and 1.57x over BSA on the SVG2 Wan 14B/720p configuration. After compliance review, we will open-source KPage and submit a pull request to NVIDIA cuDNN Frontend.
original_abstract.source_title: KPage: Cross-Block Page Compaction for Hardware-Efficient Sparse Attention

en.text: KPage addresses wasted GPU tile capacity in partially occupied sparse-attention blocks. It packs 16-row KV pages across block boundaries during loading and selects query tile shapes, preserving the original sparse graph without materializing compacted tensors in high-bandwidth memory. Across eight layouts it reports 1.13–4.25 times forward and 1.02–2.71 times forward-plus-backward speedup over the strongest exact sparse baselines. These are attention-kernel results, not recommendation-system gains.

zh.text: KPage 针对稀疏注意力块未填满造成的 GPU tile 容量浪费，在加载时跨块打包 16 行 KV 页面，并选择查询 tile 形状；它保留原稀疏图，不在高带宽显存中物化压紧后的张量。在八种布局上，前向速度为最强精确稀疏基线的 1.13–4.25 倍，前向加反向为 1.02–2.71 倍。这些是注意力内核结果，并非推荐系统收益。

original_abstract.text: A growing body of work proposes dynamic expert-skipping methods for Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models that adjust the number of experts activated per token during inference, aiming to preserve model quality while further reducing the number of active parameters. These methods have added calibrated importance scores, inter-expert similarity metrics, or learned per-token allocators in order to identify experts to skip. However, different calibration regimes, different reductions in the effective number of experts, and evaluation suites make comparisons difficult. We classify four representative prior methods into a unified taxonomy and benchmark them against a natural, simple baseline: statically reducing the number of experts $k$ (i.e., same reduced $k$ across all layers and tokens). We provide a fair comparison of these methods at matched expert-compute budget, on two modern MoEs (Gemma4-26B-A4B and Qwen3-30B-A3B) in a text-only setting and a contemporary vision-language model (Qwen3-VL) in a multimodal setting. Surprisingly, we find that the simple baseline is hard to outperform consistently across models, modalities, benchmarks, and calibration settings. The methods we benchmark often underperform the baseline and achieved gains, when present, are minor. We further find that the effective $k$ achieved (or optimized for) in calibration can diverge from the effective $k$ in testing, resulting in over- or under-estimating the compute at inference time. Based on these findings, we recommend a calibration-free per-modality static $k$ reduction and validate this on a held-out model and modality. We further argue that a static control at matched measured compute is the baseline any dynamic skipping method must beat.
original_abstract.source_title: Don't Skip the Baseline: A Controlled Comparison of Dynamic Expert Skipping in MoEs

en.text: This controlled study compares four dynamic MoE expert-skipping methods with simply reducing the same expert count across layers and tokens. At matched expert-compute budgets, static reduction is difficult to beat consistently across text and multimodal models. Calibration-time effective expert counts can diverge from test-time counts, distorting cost comparisons. The contribution is a stronger evaluation baseline, not a new recommendation architecture.

zh.text: 该受控研究将四种动态 MoE 专家跳过方法，与所有层和 token 使用相同较小专家数的简单方案比较。在专家计算预算一致时，静态减少专家数很难被文本和多模态模型上的动态方法稳定超越；校准与测试时的实际专家数还可能不同，导致成本比较失真。其价值在于建立更可靠的评测基线，并非提出新的推荐架构。

original_abstract.text: Head-dimension compression can reduce the memory required by the key-value (KV) cache, but existing methods often reconstruct full-dimensional representations during inference, adding significant decoding FLOPs overhead. We formalize the design considerations for converting pretrained attention into a natively reduced-dimensional form that reduces both KV-cache storage and attention computation using a calibration set. Specifically, we consider reductions that (1) apply a shared projection to queries and keys so that they remain in a common reduced feature space, (2) derive this projection jointly from query and key activations to better preserve their interaction, and (3) are compatible with the pretrained RoPE transformation. To obtain a reconstruction-free realization of this reduction, we restrict it to coordinate selection and theoretically show that RoPE compatibility then holds if and only if complete rotary pairs are retained. Building on this characterization, we introduce RACE, a post-training method that selects rotary pairs using their joint query-key activation energy. We theoretically show that this criterion minimizes a separable, calibration-dependent upper bound on post-RoPE query-key product approximation error. The resulting reductions are folded into the model weights and require neither runtime reconstruction nor specialized kernels. Across three model families and different compression levels, RACE outperforms structured pruning and remains competitive with reconstruction-based methods on language-modeling, zero-shot, and long-context tasks. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, RACE reduces total inference FLOPs by 47.8%, yielding 1.79x higher throughput, 43.2% lower time-to-first-token (TTFT), and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory in comparison to an uncompressed model.
original_abstract.source_title: RACE: RoPE-Aligned Attention Compression Based on Query-Key Activation Energies

en.text: RACE reduces KV-cache dimensions without reconstructing full-dimensional states at inference. It selects complete RoPE rotary pairs using joint query-key activation energy and folds the selection into model weights. At 50% KV-cache retention and 256K context, it reports 47.8% fewer total inference FLOPs, 1.79 times throughput, 43.2% lower TTFT and 28.1% lower allocated GPU memory than the uncompressed model. Recommendation transfer is untested.

zh.text: RACE 通过保留完整 RoPE 旋转对来压缩 KV 缓存维度，依据查询与键的联合激活能量选择坐标，并将选择折叠进模型权重，避免推理时重建完整表示。在保留 50% KV 缓存、256K 上下文的设置下，相对未压缩模型，总推理 FLOPs 减少 47.8%，吞吐达到 1.79 倍，首 token 延迟下降 43.2%，已分配 GPU 显存下降 28.1%。推荐任务迁移尚未验证。

original_abstract.text: Multimodal rerankers are usually dedicated models: a vision-language model (VLM) is trained on retrieval data to score the candidates of a query. Scoring options is not specific to reranking. System One decision models such as Jev map a state and a typed question to one probability per option without generating text, and general models can make such decisions with little or no training. Reranking is one such decision, with the query and its candidates as the state and the candidates as the options. We therefore argue that a general VLM can serve as a multimodal reranker through System One decisions, and that decision tuning can improve its reranking. We ask a VLM one choice question over the top 16 candidates of a first-stage retriever and rank the candidates by the probabilities of their labels, read from one forward pass. On MMEB-V2 image retrieval, this choice scores 5.4 to 7.3 hit@1 above a yes/no question per candidate, and the yes/no question falls below the first stage. With the choice, zero-shot Qwen3.8-27B beats the supervised Qwen3-VL-Reranker-2B on all three benchmarks and comes within 1.6 points of Reranker-8B on each. It matches Reranker-8B on MMEB-V2 visual documents (84.79 vs. 84.78 nDCG@5), at 1.1 to 1.5 times its latency. JEV-27B-VL, the same backbone tuned on text decisions only, improves page reranking by 0.6 to 1.1 points, with gains on most tasks (sign test, p <= 0.017), and leaves natural images unchanged. The zero-shot model is larger than the supervised rerankers and of a newer generation, so these comparisons are confounded; we discuss this and other alternative views, and the experiments that would test the position.
original_abstract.source_title: Multimodal Reranking Is a System One Decision

en.text: This study casts multimodal reranking as one multiple-choice decision over sixteen candidates, ranking label probabilities from a single VLM forward pass. It outperforms per-candidate yes/no scoring; text-only decision tuning further improves page reranking by 0.6–1.1 points while leaving natural images unchanged. Comparisons with supervised rerankers are confounded by model size and generation, so they do not isolate the proposed formulation’s effect.

zh.text: 该研究将多模态重排转化为对十六个候选的一次多选决策，用视觉语言模型单次前向计算的标签概率排序。它优于逐候选的是非问答打分；仅用文本决策调优后，页面重排再提高 0.6–1.1 点，自然图像效果未变。与监督式重排器的比较受到模型大小和代际差异干扰，不能单独归因于这一决策形式。

original_abstract.text: Large Language Model inference over long contexts is increasingly bottlenecked by the cost of attending to a growing Key-Value (KV) cache. Sparse attention reduces this cost by accessing only a fraction of the cache, but existing methods face a trade-off between deterministic retrieval, which captures high-scoring tokens but discards residual attention mass, and sampling, which improves coverage at the cost of higher variance. Hybrid methods combine top-$k$ retrieval with uniform sampling, yet still exhibit a substantial gap from dense attention at aggressive sparsity. We introduce \emph{Stratified Sparse Attention (SSA)}, a unified framework combining deterministic retrieval with score-guided sampling. SSA deterministically attends to high-scoring tokens while sampling the residual using proxy attention scores and correcting for their inclusion probabilities, thereby recovering attention mass beyond the retrieval set. SSA encompasses top-$k$, top-$p$, and hybrid top-$k$+sampling as special cases. Across RULER, LongBench, LOFT, and AIME, and five models ranging from 3B to 27B parameters, SSA consistently improves over the baselines at matched sparsity. On RULER-HARD with Ministral-3-8B, SSA improves accuracy over the strongest practical baseline from 81.8\% to 84.2\% at 32K and from 63.8\% to 69.3\% at 128K under $50\times$ attention sparsity, recovering 94\% and 85\% of dense-attention performance, respectively. With optimized CUDA kernels, SSA achieves up to $2.96\times$ decode speedup over FlashInfer at 1M context, demonstrating that its accuracy gains translate into practical long-context inference acceleration. We open-source our code at https://github.com/skylight-org/SSA-Paper-Code.
original_abstract.source_title: Stratified Sparse Attention: Reducing the Sparse-to-Dense Gap at Extreme Sparsity

en.text: Stratified Sparse Attention combines deterministic retrieval of high-score tokens with score-guided sampling and inclusion-probability correction for residual attention mass. Across five language models and four benchmark suites, it improves accuracy at matched sparsity. Optimized CUDA kernels yield up to 2.96 times decode speedup over FlashInfer at one-million-token context. The evidence concerns language-model inference; recommendation transfer remains untested.

zh.text: Stratified Sparse Attention 将高分 token 的确定性检索与分数引导的剩余部分采样结合，再按入选概率校正遗漏的注意力质量。在五个语言模型和四组基准上，它在相同稀疏度下改善准确率；优化后的 CUDA 内核在百万 token 上下文中实现最高 2.96 倍于 FlashInfer 的解码速度。证据来自语言模型推理，尚未验证推荐任务迁移。
